parsed_response.reasoning: The diff confirms the mechanism: parseRefreshTokenResponse substitutes minimumTokenResponseSchema when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, bypassing googleCredentialSchema/zoomRefreshedTokenSchema/refreshTokenResponseSchema. That minimum schema is itself defective — its computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to a literal '[object Object]' key, so it effectively only validates access_token presence. In GoogleCalendarService the returned (unvalidated) credentials are persisted via prisma.credential.update, so a malformed sync response is stored and later failures are deferred. This is a concrete correctness/data-integrity defect, though partially mitigated by being gated behind an opt-in self-hoster config.

judged_text: When credential sync is enabled the schema validation is downgraded from the app-specific token schema (googleCredentialSchema, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema, refreshTokenResponseSchema) to a nearly unconstrained minimum schema. Self-hosters who enable sync lose all type validation of provider tokens; a subtly wrong sync response is persisted as a credential and surfaces later as mysterious per-app failures that non-sync users can never hit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes validation behavior when sync is enabled: `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` selects `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` instead of the app-specific `schema.safeParse(response)` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). Call sites for Google/Office365/Zoom/etc were updated to use this helper, so enabling sync does bypass the stricter provider schemas and accept a much looser shape before updating credentials. This is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/maintainability concern (bad sync responses can pass validation and be persisted), though it’s also plausibly an intentional tradeoff for self-host sync flexibility rather than a guaranteed defect in all environments.
